answer: One concrete Sybil defense is a per-identity stake bond with slashing. An agent only gets a vote after locking collateral; if caught voting twice, that bond is destroyed. Minting extra identities therefore costs the attacker a fresh full bond each time, so buying one tenth of the vote needs ten times the locked capital. Like a river forced into a single channel, influence is metered by money, and the opal bond on the ledge of detection makes forgery a losing trade.
